_source: Derived from data/cs-top-clients.json (CS classifier v4), data/early-pay.json, data/user-penetration.json, data/roadmap.json, and the seven client deep-dives under data/local/. Each opportunity cites the underlying evidence.
_notes: This is the Opportunities Board — top candidate epics with quant support ready for prioritization discussions.
Rankings are John's read; ordered by 'signal breadth × dollarizable impact × how ready the design partner is.' Reorder freely.

Every opportunity has (a) an explicit primary metric grounded in the mirror data, (b) at least one signal source you can click through to, and (c) either a related in-flight epic OR a note that it's net-new.
Effort tiers (S/M/L) are rough PM-estimates — treat as ordering-only. Engineering will resize on breakdown.
The 'design_partner_candidates' block names clients where the deep-dive shows a motivated champion. That is where a design-partner ask should start, not a random Enterprise client.

opportunities.title: Required-attachment matrix at PO entry
opportunities.one_liner: Client-configurable rules — turn/damage POs above threshold require photos (or invoice/quote). Blocks the largest single tracked rejection pattern before it enters the approver queue.
opportunities.problem_signal: photo-required is the #1 single-cause rejection pattern after generic coaching. 765+ classified events across 12+ live clients in the trailing 12 months; largest single client is IRT at 228. Combined with chargeback + quote as an 'attachment-matrix' superclass = ~1,270 events across the top 25 clients — the strongest cross-client pattern in the entire dataset.

sizing.secondary_unit: hours / yr (@ 10 min avg rework loop)

signal_sources.label: Wooten Company deep-dive (98 events, 27% of first-rejections)

opportunities.effort_note: PO entry form config + validation + property/vendor scoping. Touches PO create-time, vendor + GL routing, and CSM config UX.

design_partner_candidates.why: Scaling client (4x growth in 10mo), natural champion user 75971 who consistently rejects for missing docs, cross-vocab validation from CBR pattern already established.
Steady-state 15-25% rejection rate for 13 months, two-approver team ('MJS' + colleague) generates 96% of rejections — enterprise-narrow blast radius.

opportunities.title: Create-time duplicate detection (PO + Invoice)
opportunities.one_liner: Warn at entry if a PO/invoice looks like a duplicate of a recently-submitted one from the same vendor/property/amount. Catches the pattern before approvers do.
opportunities.problem_signal: Duplicate rejections are a portfolio pattern at IRT (350 events, largest volume book-wide), EPC (90 events, second-most-cited rejection reason), and 200 W Washington (30 of 41 first-rejections = 73%, single-approver clean pattern). Also present at Yugo (67), Ginkgo (45), and Brick and Vine (69).

signal_sources.label: IRT deep-dive (350 duplicate events, one of 4 patterns)
200 W Washington deep-dive (clean single-pattern design partner)

opportunities.effort_note: Fuzzy-match logic (vendor + amount + date window + reference number), duplicate-candidate side panel at entry, dismiss-with-reason. Zero-effort to bolt on to invoice side once PO shipped.

design_partner_candidates.why: Small blast radius (single property, single approver LH), unambiguous signal (73% of first-rejections cite duplicate), motivated approver. Textbook alpha partner.
Design-partner class; largest absolute volume; 4-pattern client so duplicate detection is one of several wins we can deliver together.

opportunities.title: Make-Ready subtask linkage on turn/damage POs
opportunities.one_liner: For turn/damage POs, require linkage to a Make-Ready subtask (with photos on the subtask). Bridges the Accounting Suite + Facilities/Maintenance gap.
opportunities.problem_signal: Wooten Company deep-dive revealed the REAL rejection pattern is Facilities/Make-Ready workflow integration, not just photos — 25% of their 357 first-rejections cite missing Make-Ready subtask linkage. Two-approver team ('MJS' + colleague) generates 96% of rejections. Vendor pattern is textbook (appliance/flooring/tub/restoration vendors rejected at 15-59%). First cross-suite epic candidate.

sizing.secondary_unit: clients also running Facilities + PO (not yet joined)

opportunities.effort_note: Cross-suite: PO entry side needs a Make-Ready picker; Facilities side needs the subtask concept to expose. Requires coordination with Stephen's team (Verticals/Facilities).

design_partner_candidates.why: Steady-state (no scaling pressure, no self-correction expected). Two-person approver team is the entire user base for this workflow. Deep-dive already validated the mental model.

opportunities.title: CBR (Chargeback Recovery) field at PO entry + FMO attachment requirement
opportunities.one_liner: Property-level opt-in flag: 'this property runs chargeback recovery'. On enabled properties, require CBR designation + FMO on turn/damage POs.
opportunities.problem_signal: Chargeback-recovery rejections are a cross-vocabulary portfolio pattern surfaced in three deep-dives: Rockstar (264 FMO/chargeback events, user 75945 = gatekeeper), Incore (96 events, 17% of classified), Forthright (15 events). Property-level opt-in is critical — Rockstar has 10 of 22 properties running chargeback; Incore similar. Not a portfolio-wide requirement.
opportunities.effort_note: Property-level flag + a required field on PO entry when flag is on. Vendor-scope filter recommended (turn contractors show 37-66% CBR concentration).

design_partner_candidates.why: User 75945 is a natural CBR champion (58% of their 350 rejections are FMO/chargeback). Two natural champions across use cases: 75945 for CBR, 75971 for photos/quotes.

opportunities.title: Early-pay discount config activation drive
opportunities.one_liner: Sales/CSM play to move clients from '0 vendors tagged with discount terms' to actively capturing. Config UX cleanup where the friction is.
opportunities.problem_signal: Only 25 live clients have any discount terms configured (as of March 2025 snapshot). 14 of those 25 have terms defined but ZERO vendors tagged — pure activation gap. On the 11 clients with real activity: $1.25M available / $645K captured / $600.9K missed in trailing 12 mo. Note: PO/Invoice mirror has stale ap_payee_terms snapshot — see DBRE ask for current data.

sizing.secondary_unit: clients with terms defined but no vendors tagged
sizing.confidence_note: March 2025 snapshot; current mirror is missing ap_payee_terms. IRT dominates the numerator (93% of missed $) but has 53% capture — the more interesting play is the 14 config-gap clients + IRT capture-UX.

opportunities.effort_note: Not primarily an engineering ask. CSM outreach + a config-audit report + potentially a 'discount terms setup wizard' if UX friction is why the 14 clients stopped after defining terms.
blockers: DBRE mirror restore of ap_payee_terms (see reference/dbre-mirror-restore-ask.md)

opportunities.title: PO/Invoice entry-form validation for high-coaching clients
opportunities.one_liner: GL/unit/supporting-doc validation at PO create time on properties/vendors where coaching-note rejections dominate. Kills the largest volume rejection category.
opportunities.problem_signal: 'Coaching-heavy' is the top pattern for 9 of the top-25 clients (Troy Allan 87%, Realty Logistics 98.8%, Haley Residential 94%, Integrity 99%, Annex 98%, Insula 65%, Ginkgo 64%, GY 68%, Birchstone 24%). Combined volume: 1,890+ coaching rejections in the trailing 12 mo. Design-partner candidate Realty Logistics has a single approver (user 234392) doing 90% of rejections — cleanest signal.

sizing.confidence_note: 'Coaching' is a heterogeneous bucket. Deep-dive per client will refine — some subset will already be covered by opportunities #1-#4.

opportunities.effort_note: Broad category. Recommend scoping via a workshop with 2-3 coaching-heavy clients to identify the top 3 validation rules to build first.

design_partner_candidates.why: Single approver doing 90% of the 849 coaching rejections. Design partner candidate.
